prior_importants.description: `HEADING` runs on every line outside a fence. Its lazy capture is followed by `\s*#*\s*$`, so a single line like `# a` + N spaces + `b` costs about N³/6 backtracking steps and blocks the event loop of whatever process runs intake.

PLACEHOLDER only matches the bare token, so in a terse field a placeholder with a trailing period or Markdown wrapping passes as filled: Affected area `TBD.`, Suspected area `Unknown.`, Source PR `N/A.` or Time box `` `n/a` `` are reported complete, while the same text without the period is flagged vague.

EMPTY_LIST_ITEM is tested with the `m` flag across the whole field, code fences included, so any pasted unified diff that adds or removes a blank line (a line that is just `+` or `-`) marks a fully filled Reproduction, Expected against actual, Findings, Scenarios or Proof field as vague.

A path-like glob such as `src/**/*.ts` or `src/**` in `Files in scope` (the form asks for "One path or glob per line") becomes the single module `**` and matches no ADR glob, so a repo-wide refactor fires neither trigger.

Follow-up has no `area` field, so its whole body feeds the triggers. The scope globs and paths used as inputs in `Scenarios` then fire adr-area or module-boundary falsely. `Findings`, which the form defines as "the file and line it points at", is the real area field.

moduleOf's new rule (no extension in the last segment means a directory) treats a test-helper path ending in a sentence period, or a wildcard under test/<kind>/, as a module. That gives a false module-boundary trigger and a design the ticket doesn't need.

For chore and refactor, `Scope boundary` is marked `area: true`. Both the form and the rubric ask that field to name what the change leaves alone, so paths the ticket stays out of fire the module-boundary and ADR-area triggers.

When the area names a file by its GitHub permalink, the extracted path starts with `github.com/<owner>/<repo>/blob/<ref>/`. That path matches no ADR glob and no module, so `adr-area` and `module-boundary` don't fire and the design gate passes when it should fail.

findings.description: The new `.replace(/\.+$/, '')` runs on each PATH match. A match with a long run of dots that is not at its end takes quadratic time. One `a/<65,530 dots>x` in an area field costs about 2.1e9 start-and-backtrack steps of V8 irregexp time on the event loop. PATH itself handles this input in linear time, so the cost comes only from this delta.
findings.body:
**ReDoS: the new trailing-period strip is quadratic on a dot run inside a path**

```ts
const paths = (areaText.match(PATH) ?? []).map((path) =>
  path.replace(/^\.\//, '').replace(/\.+$/, ''),
);
```

`/\.+$/` has no start anchor, so irregexp tries a match at every dot. PATH's segments (`[\w.-]+` and `[\w.*-]+`) accept any number of dots, so one PATH match can hold a long dot run followed by a non-dot.

**Trigger:** a bug whose `Suspected area` is `a/` + N dots + `x`. Any area field works, and so does anywhere in a follow-up body, since that type is read whole.
- **PATH is linear on this input.** It returns the single match `a/....x` after one O(N) backoff. The earlier PATH concern needs input with no slash, and this input is not that case.
- **`/\.+$/` is quadratic on that match.** From each dot, the greedy `\.+` runs to `x`, then backs off one dot at a time, and `$` fails at every step. V8's end-anchor shortcut only applies when the maximum match length is under 1024, and `\.+` has no bound. Node's linear fallback engine is off by default.
- **Total:** about N²/2 steps. GitHub caps an issue body at 65,536 characters, so N can reach about 65,530, which is about 2.1e9 steps: seconds of blocked event loop on every check. The author can edit the body after `ready`, so the check can be made to run again.

Before this delta, the input was linear end to end.

**Fix:** a lookbehind lets a match start only at the first dot of a run. Every other start fails in O(1), so the strip runs in linear time. It still removes every trailing dot, and an all-dot string still becomes empty.

<https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/pupitre/blob/f1b1927eb2968f4d80e2dabc6fd8397876be97ea/src/core/ticket-intake.utils.ts#L169-L171>

process_issues.description: Consolidator not spawned: the reviewers returned a single finding in total, so there was nothing to group. review-simplicity was skipped because the delta adds no file, helper, option or branch. Context, maintainability, spec and workflow-safety were skipped because their gates did not hold.
The conventions reviewer reported that it did not open general.md or naming.md before concluding there were no findings, so any rule from those docs was checked only from memory.
